g1.necessity: Convergence lifecycle previously had no explicit boundary: tool calls could be declared into the WAL after the model had already signaled terminal intent, and extreme compaction could drop interjected human turns. A mechanical boundary plus fenced tool cycle is required so terminal intent, WAL declaration order, and human interjection preservation are invariants rather than conventions.

g2.authority_owner: ConvergenceBoundaryService (engine_services/convergence_boundary.py) owns boundary state; the engine/tool_cycle consult it before dispatch and before WAL declaration; convergence_decide is the single builtin allowed across a pending boundary.
g2.non_duplication: Not a replacement: prior run finalization paths remain; the boundary adds the missing lifecycle authority and does not duplicate recovery_controller or run_finalizer responsibilities (those act after run end; the boundary acts during the terminal window).

model_evidence: not_applicable: deterministic lifecycle machinery; tests assert state transitions, WAL prune order, and byte-exact interjection survival without model judgment
g3.recovery_or_reason: Boundary violations fail closed: non-decide calls are pruned with explicit error events; recovery re-enters the normal loop path.

g4.rollback: Revert the convergence guard commit range; deployed rollback must publish a prior clean code root as a new service-control generation.
verification: full repository CI on PR head
